stemMd:
Five presentations, F, G, H, J and K, are scheduled one per day from Monday to Friday of the same week.

- G is scheduled on an earlier day than J.
- H is on Wednesday or Thursday.
- K is not on the day immediately before or immediately after H.
- F is on Monday or Friday.

Which of the following **could** be true?

options.label: C
options.textMd: F is on Friday and G is on Wednesday.

explanationMd:
Split on H, since it has only two possible days.

- **H on Wednesday.** K cannot be on Tuesday or Thursday, so K is on Monday or Friday. F also needs Monday or Friday, so F and K take those two days between them. G and J take Tuesday and Thursday, with G on Tuesday because it comes first. Two schedules: K, G, H, J, F and F, G, H, J, K.
- **H on Thursday.** K cannot be on Wednesday or Friday, so K is on Monday or Tuesday. If F is on Monday, K is on Tuesday and G, J fill Wednesday and Friday: F, K, G, H, J. If F is on Friday, K and G, J share Monday to Wednesday: K, G, J, H, F or G, K, J, H, F.

That gives five possible schedules. The schedule F, K, G, H, J puts J on Friday, so that statement could be true.

Test each of the others against the list, or directly:

- G on Thursday forces J onto Friday and H onto Wednesday; then K needs Monday or Friday, Friday is taken, and F cannot have either end day.
- J on Tuesday forces G onto Monday and F onto Friday; H and K are left with Wednesday and Thursday, which are adjacent.
- K on Thursday is adjacent to H on Wednesday, and H cannot also be on Thursday.
- F on Friday with G on Wednesday leaves Thursday for both H and J, since J must come after G.

What to notice first: in a "could be true" question, build the short list of complete schedules first; then each choice is a quick look-up.

distractorRationale.d: With G on Thursday, J must be on Friday and H on Wednesday. K then needs Monday or Friday, so it takes Monday, and F has neither end day available.
distractorRationale.e: With J on Tuesday, G must be on Monday, so F is on Friday. H and K are left with Wednesday and Thursday, which are consecutive days, breaking the condition on K.
distractorRationale.b: K on Thursday is next to Wednesday, and H must be on Wednesday once Thursday is taken. The condition on K and H rules this out.
distractorRationale.c: With F on Friday and G on Wednesday, J must come after Wednesday, so J is on Thursday; but H also needs Wednesday or Thursday, and both are taken.

accessibilityText: Five presentations named by the letters F, G, H, J and K are scheduled one per day, Monday to Friday. G is earlier than J; H is on Wednesday or Thursday; K is not on a day next to H's day; F is on Monday or Friday. The question asks which statement could be true. Five answer choices.

independentSolve.workingNotes: A possible: F Mon, K Tue, G Wed, H Thu, J Fri (K not adjacent to H, G<J). B: K Thu adjacent to H whether H Wed or conflicts with H Thu. C: G Wed forces H Thu, J would need Thu/Fri - both taken. D: G Thu forces J Fri, F Mon, H Wed, K Tue adjacent to H. E: J Tue forces G Mon, F Fri, K in Wed/Thu adjacent to H.
